brief: Tells the facts of the running program (identity, uptime, memory, machine) and manages one child process: spawn, stream, wait, kill.
detail: Without a child, an object reads the running program: its id, uptime on a monotonic clock, memory, processor time, architecture, operating system and byte order, all delegated to the engine. Spawn starts a child through the platform shell and SpawnIn starts one from an argument list with no shell; both are effectful and start a real program. The usage contract avoids a pipe deadlock: read the child's output to its end, then Wait, then Free. Kill ends the child whose handle the object holds and never looks a process up by name. WaitFor, IsRunning and SpawnIn need an engine built from the current source; an older stz_system.dll lacks them and raises R3.
